title: Public inquest into 2010 Saskatoon cell death to begin December
subtitle: There will be a public inquest into the death of a man who was arrested for public intoxication in Saskatoon a...
article: There will be a public inquest into the death of a man who was arrested for public intoxication in Saskatoon a few years ago.
Stanley Robillard, 46, was arrested for being drunk in public on July 15, 2010. He was taken to a cell at the Saskatoon Police Service Detention Centre.
Robillard was found unresponsive in his cell the next day. He was taken to the Royal University Hospital where he died.

The Chief Coroner is required to hold an inquest into the death of any person who dies in a jail or correctional facility. The exception to the Coroners Act is if the coroner is satisfied that the person's death was natural causes and not preventable.

"The purpose of an inquest is to provide a public hearing to examine in detail the events surrounding a death. In addition to establishing the medical cause of death and the manner of death, the coroner's jury may make recommendations to prevent similar deaths in the future," a government news release said.
Coroner Brent Gough of Saskatoon will preside at the inquest.
